main_text.p: » te tempora Augusti, inquit, » publicè respondendi ius non » à Principib. dabatur: sed qui » fiduciā studiorum suorū ha- » bebāt, consulentibus respon- » debant: neque responsa uti- » que signata dabāt, sed plerun- » que iudicibus ipsi scribebāt, » aut testabantur qui illos con- » sulebant. Erat autem duplex huiusce scientiae profitendae ratio: cum aut transuerso fo- ro ambulantes, aut domi in folio, hoc est, magnifica & honorabili sella confidentès, omnibus consuledi sui potestatem se facere demonstrarent. Cuius rei testimonio est hic ex lib. de Orat. III. Cicero

page.notes: The » marks at the start of each line are printed quotation marks and are kept as printed. "Cicero" is followed by the catchword "nis" at lower right, the first syllable of "Ciceronis". The running head is decorative and too damaged to read. Doubtful readings: "confidentès" and "consuledi" are as printed, with the printed accent and spelling kept. The page has no margin notes.
